title: Replay and price individual and coded BIT chart-267 receiver exchanges
body:
Four literal receiver exchanges preserve both 680-owner operators. All pay extra grade-two crossings across the 36 native calls. The new topology and exact before-read stock checks establish the price of these repairs.

## Scope and source

Uses #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`, the chart-267 geometry, and the named chart-349/374 readers. The proof covers its single-direction cuts and constructed exchanges. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit267-receiver-exchange/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. The archived README lists the exact offline command. The local clean replay checked all four complete operators, the directed invoice and corrupted controls. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

A different joint recoding would need a realizable stock path and a positive full 36-call invoice. Native and application qualification remain conditional.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
